title: Phase-gate traffic choreography microflow
creator: Sofia Delgado
description:
Goal: Design a compact, keyboard-friendly microflow within the Redwood Console that enables engineers and product managers to orchestrate phase-gated traffic shifts (canary -> progressive -> full) with clear safety affordances and a one-click escape hatch. The microflow must surface signal windows, suggested gate durations, automatic rollback thresholds, and quick manual rollback actions without taking users away from the main rollout timeline.

Scope: prototype a compact matrix UI (phase x audience segment) + an inline guardrail card that shows active signals (latency/error/cost), a predicted risk score, and suggested mitigation actions. Include microinteractions for previewing simulated traffic splits, a condensed confirm UX for emergency rollback, and keyboard shortcuts for power users. Provide a 2-state compact and expanded detail view for desktop and a single streamlined mobile flow for on-call access.

Out of scope: full experiment analytics dashboard and backend routing policies (ENG implements). This ticket is design-first: deliver Figma screens, an interactive prototype demonstrating the emergency rollback flow, copy for microcopy and toast messaging, and a short usability script for 5 rapid moderated sessions.
acceptance_criteria: Figma prototype shows compact matrix (phase x segment) + inline guardrail card flow
Emergency rollback flow completes in 3 taps or via single keyboard shortcut in prototype
Prototype includes simulated telemetry overlays that update splits and show predicted risk
Copy includes clear guardrail language and post-rollback toasts/messages
Usability script ready and at least 5 moderated sessions planned before handoff
comments: 2025-02-11 - Sofia Delgado: Kickoff notes — met with PM (Rina Patel) and ENG lead (Arjun Rao). Consensus to keep matrix compact to reduce cognitive load during incidents. ENG asked for precise props for automated suggestions (threshold defaults) — added ENG-88077 as dependency.

2025-02-15 - Markus Chen: First wireframes posted to Figma link. Focused on a 3-column compact matrix: audience | current split | next phase target. Left a placeholder for guardrail card. Requesting API shape from Arjun to render live signal indicators in prototype (latency, error rate, cost delta).

2025-02-20 - Arjun Rao (engineering): Provided mock telemetry endpoints and suggested default rollback thresholds: 5% error increase over baseline OR 20% latency p95 regress. Will expose an array of signals. ENG:92110 will consume these props for simulation harness.

2025-02-24 - Rina Patel (PM): Review feedback — unify 'escape hatch' verbiage to 'Emergency Rollback' and reduce the number of confirmation steps. PM wants visible audit trail entry after any manual rollback. Added requirement to show last 24h signal context inline.

2025-02-27 - UX Research (Linh Tran): Drafted 5-minute moderated usability script targeting SREs. Hypothesis: emergency rollback must be discoverable and runnable within 90 seconds. Scheduling sessions for 2025-03-03 to 03-07.

2025-03-02 - Design review @ 1pm: Internal feedback from Eng and PM — iterate on affordances for keyboard users (add 'r' for rollback hotkey) and low-vision accessibility (high-contrast guardrail card variant). Marking for accessibility pass.

2025-03-04 - Prototype update: Added simulated split preview animations and a condensed rollback confirmation modal with optional notes field. Adjusted microcopy to include reason suggestions from policy templates. Submitted for engineering review: GitHub PR #322.

2025-03-05 - Markus Chen: Ran first internal simulation with ENG test harness — risk score correlates to simulated error bursts in expected way. Small UX gap: users wanted an intermediate 'preview effects' state before committing to roll forward; added a 'Preview impact' CTA in the matrix that animates split change on simulated traffic for 6s. Tagging for final review ahead of handoff.
review_feedback: PM (Rina Patel) — Approve if audit trail is auto-attached and escape hatch is single-action with undo window
Eng (Arjun Rao) — Need deterministic API contract for signals; suggest adding a lightweight JSON schema to the PR
Security (Priya Nair) — Ensure rollback action is recorded in event store and triggers existing RBAC checks. Security review flagged but not blocking (see DES-4213 for RBAC patterns)
Accessibility (Sam O'Shea) — High-contrast variant required; focus state for keyboard ordering must land on emergency rollback button last to avoid accidental triggers
next_steps: Incorporate security and accessibility recommendations into Figma (owner: Markus) — due 2025-03-10
Complete 5 usability sessions and synthesize findings into one-pager (owner: Linh) — sessions 2025-03-03..03-07
Finalize API contract file and attach JSON schema to PR #322 (owner: Arjun) — target 2025-03-09
Handoff package: Figma files, prototype link, copy spec, usability one-pager, and acceptance criteria checklist — planned handoff 2025-03-12
notes: Unique constraints considered: must be operable under paging conditions (single-handed mobile flow), minimal context switching, and provide a reversible emergency experience. The microflow intentionally reduces modal depth and adds an ephemeral undo toast with a 30s window to revert automated rollbacks. Prototype emphasizes clarity of cause (which signal triggered rollback) to help postmortem investigations.
